text.p: A new strong storm tracks across the northern British Isles and into the southern Norway coast during today, tonight and Tuesday. Very strong winds will likely impact much of the British Isles and southern Norway. Strong winds will also impact the north coast of France and Benelux during this time. Seas from the north Atlantic to the North Sea and the English Channel will also be impacted. Very strong winds and very rough seas make it very hazzardous for ships in the region.

Tropical Cyclone 27S is moving away from the Australia coast as it slowly begins to weekend. The threat of flooding to the Australia coast is now greatly reduced. The risk during the next 24 hours will be mainly to shipping and even this risk will diminish as the system weakens and dissipates late in the period.
Tropical cyclone Karlette is still a risk to shipping over the open water well south of Mauritius during the next 12-24 hours. This system sould become extratropical within the next 24-36 hours.

Tropical cyclone Ita formed east of the Queensland Australia coast and moved rapidly inland during the past 12 hours. It had winds of only 40 mph as it moved inland. It may have caused some minor coastal flooding as the time of landfall. This system is already dissipating as it tracks further inland.
